metadata.title: 1977 Case 50
metadata.original_presentation: A 76-year-old man was admitted to the hospital because of renal failure. He was well until four months earlier, when he experienced transient bilateral paresthesia with questionable dysarthria.

required.content: What is the patient's medical history and recent symptoms?
required.response: The patient experienced transient bilateral paresthesia with questionable dysarthria four months ago. Two months before admission, he lost consciousness while parking his car and was prescribed warfarin. Eighteen days before entry, his left arm began to shake, and he became weak on the left side. He has a history of hypertension, cholelithiasis, and a duodenal ulcer with bleeding.

teaching_points.content: Transient neurological symptoms can be indicative of transient ischemic attacks or other cerebrovascular events.
Warfarin is an anticoagulant used to prevent thromboembolic events, but it requires careful monitoring to avoid complications.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Warfarin-induced bleeding
supporting_evidence: history of duodenal ulcer with bleeding
refuting_evidence: no direct evidence of bleeding complications presented

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Parkinson's Disease
refuting_evidence: no mention of bradykinesia or rigidity

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Hypertensive Encephalopathy
refuting_evidence: no mention of severe hypertension at presentation

required.content: What were the findings on physical examination upon admission?
required.response: The patient was somnolent and confused. Funduscopic examination revealed slight to moderate arterial narrowing. No rash, petechiae, or ecchymoses were seen. The jugular venous pressure was 4 cm. The lungs were clear, and the heart was normal with a Grade 1 systolic ejection murmur along the left sternal border. The femoral pulses were ++, and the posterior tibial pulses were absent; the right dorsalis pedis pulse was absent, and the left ++. Abdominal examination was negative; no flank tenderness was found, and no bony tenderness was observed. Rectal examination disclosed that the prostate gland was three times the normal size and smooth. Neurologic examination was negative except for asterixis.

teaching_points.content: Asterixis is a sign of metabolic encephalopathy, often associated with liver or renal failure.
Absent peripheral pulses can indicate peripheral vascular disease or embolic events.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) secondary to Hypertension
Warfarin-induced bleeding
key_features: history of duodenal ulcer with bleeding
additional_information_needed: CT scan of the head to rule out intracranial hemorrhage

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Atherosclerotic Peripheral Vascular Disease
supporting_evidence: absent posterior tibial and dorsalis pedis pulses

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Prostatic Hypertrophy
supporting_evidence: prostate gland three times the normal size

required.content: What were the key laboratory and imaging findings?
required.response: The hematocrit was 29.7%, white-cell count 6600, with 64% neutrophils. The urea nitrogen was 147 mg, creatinine 9.5 mg, uric acid 17.5 mg. Electrocardiogram showed left ventricular hypertrophy. Chest X-ray revealed a slightly unfolded aorta with calcification. CT scan of the brain showed enlarged lateral ventricles. Lumbar puncture yielded clear cerebrospinal fluid with 8 red cells, no white cells, glucose 65 mg, protein 40 mg.

teaching_points.content: Elevated creatinine and urea nitrogen levels are indicative of renal impairment.
Left ventricular hypertrophy on ECG can be a result of long-standing hypertension.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) secondary to Hypertension
Cerebrovascular Accident (CVA) or Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA)
refuting_evidence: negative neurologic examination except for asterixis

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Warfarin-induced bleeding
key_features: history of duodenal ulcer with bleeding
supporting_evidence: history of duodenal ulcer with bleeding

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Aortic Atherosclerosis with Peripheral Vascular Disease
supporting_evidence: absent posterior tibial and right dorsalis pedis pulses
calcification of aorta on chest X-ray

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Prostatic Hypertrophy
supporting_evidence: prostate gland three times normal size

required.content: What treatments were administered during the hospital stay?
required.response: The patient was given chlorthalidone, sodium bicarbonate, aluminum hydroxide, humidified oxygen, glucose in water, and a low-protein diet. Peritoneal dialysis was initiated. Diazepam, methyldopa, and hydralazine were administered to control blood pressure.

teaching_points.content: Peritoneal dialysis is used to manage severe renal failure and remove waste products from the blood.
Blood pressure control is crucial in patients with renal failure to prevent further kidney damage.

final_diagnosis.name: Chronic kidney disease with hypertensive crisis
